messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — streaming/v1 p99 latency > SLO for 10m. p95=470ms p99=2.1s. source=telemetry. runbook: https://runbooks/internal/streaming-latency

nate (oncall): ack. joining. pulling traces + batcher stats now.

emily: seeing same spike. p95 jumped 160 -> 470ms last 10m, p99 250 -> 2.1s. traces show large batches containing one very long sequence mixed with many short ones. head-of-line appears likely.

emily: dumping top batcher metrics:
```
continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size: 96 -> 178
continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens: 128k
streaming.active_long_sequences: 42 (spike)
packet_drop_rate: 0.1%
```

josh: support reports ~3 customers saw streaming stalls/timeouts in last 20m, no 5xx surge. they timed out client-side at ~60s.

sara: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 64, 2) enable seq-length preemption / fair scheduling, 3) shift a small percentage of streaming traffic to low-latency pool. which do we want immediate?

priya: preference = small config flips first (1+2). shifting traffic is safer but takes longer to route. note cost/throughput tradeoff when reducing batch size.

nate (oncall): applying option 1+2 now. patching config (rolling):
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap continuous-batcher -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"64","fair_sched":"true","preempt_long_seq":"true"}}'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher
```

ops-bot: Deploy started: rollout/continuous-batcher v2026.03.17-ops-12, rollout_id=rl-5532-1. Notifying schedulers.

emily: initial post-change numbers (2m after): p95=185ms p99=430ms. avg_batch_size down to 72. still seeing tail isolates where very long seqs hold a worker for ~1.8s.

josh: confirm customer timeouts dropped — support sees no new timeout tickets in last 10m.

sara: next-tier mitigation if residual persists: enable seq-length routing (route requests with seq_len>2000 to dedicated pool) + KV cache eviction tuning to free memory.

priya: logging action items:
- short-term: reduce max_batch_size + enable fair_sched/preempt (done)
- mid-term: implement seq-length routing policy and safer ember of long-seq pool
- postmortem: tune default max_batch_tokens and add evals for mixed-seqlen workloads

nate (oncall): monitoring 15m window. will escalate if p99 > 600ms. handing monitoring to josh at 5532110750 for the next shift. josh, please continue metrics watch and coordinate with infra if any regression.

josh: ack, I'm on it. will follow-up with a short incident summary for the postmortem and tag metric graphs.

emily: attaching quick trace snippet showing batch composition:
```json
[{"batch_id":"b-9a1","seq_lengths":[34,12,10240,18],"latencies_ms":[8,7,1800,9]}]
```

priya: note for postmortem: add a synthetic long-seq load test to CI to catch mixing regressions. also check scheduling fairness histograms over last 24h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT update: p99 reduced to 420ms (5m window). paging remains active until oncall confirms stabilization.

nate (oncall): thanks all. closing active mitigation unless we see a relapse. will file a follow-up ticket for seq-length routing and postmortem. :thumbsup:
